answer: The original source is Freddie Mac, from its Primary Mortgage Market Survey (PMMS). It is published weekly (week ending Thursday), in percent, not seasonally adjusted. FRED series MORTGAGE30US, which runs from 1971-04-02 to 2026-10-08 as of today.

The source is S&P Dow Jones Indices LLC. FRED's copy only holds a rolling 10 years of daily closes under its agreement with S&P: as of 2026-10-10 the first observation is 2016-10-10 (2163.66) and the latest is 2026-10-09. FRED series SP500 (daily close, index, price only, no dividends).

The source is S&P Dow Jones Indices LLC. FRED now titles the series the S&P Cotality Case-Shiller U.S. National Home Price Index (formerly S&P CoreLogic Case-Shiller). FRED series CSUSHPINSA: monthly, index with Jan 2000=100, not seasonally adjusted, from January 1987.

It comes from the University of Michigan's Surveys of Consumers. FRED series UMCSENT: monthly, index with 1966:Q1=100, not seasonally adjusted, from November 1952. At the university's request, FRED's copy is delayed by one month.

The source is the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA), from its Spot Prices release. FRED series DCOILWTICO (WTI at Cushing, Oklahoma): daily, dollars per barrel, not seasonally adjusted, from 1986-01-02.

The source is the U.S. Employment and Training Administration, part of the Department of Labor, in its Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims Report. Yes, the headline series is seasonally adjusted. FRED series ICSA: weekly (week ending Saturday), number of claims, from 1967-01-07.
Real GDP is reported in billions of chained 2017 dollars, at a seasonally adjusted annual rate, quarterly. The source is the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis. FRED series GDPC1.

It is an index with base period 1982-1984=100 (the average of those years equals 100), not a dollar or percent figure. The source is the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. FRED series CPIAUCSL (all items, U.S. city average): monthly, seasonally adjusted.

It is published jointly by the U.S. Census Bureau and the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), in the New Residential Sales release. FRED series MSPUS: quarterly, dollars, not seasonally adjusted, from 1963. Note that it covers new houses only; FRED's current title is 'Median Sales Price of New Houses Sold for the United States'.

FRED lists the source as the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, from its H.15 Selected Interest Rates release. FRED series DFF: daily (7-day), percent, not seasonally adjusted, from 1954-07-01; FEDFUNDS is the monthly-average version. Not from FRED: the underlying rate is calculated by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York and then published by the Board in H.15.
